title: Context assembly plane — the last hop, where accuracy-per-token is actually won or lost
description:
Last of seven plane epics (see `project-management/design/ADVANCED_MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `project-management/AI_NATIVE_AGILE.md`).

**Invariant this plane owns:** the output fits the token budget and is ordered for the U-curve.

Every other plane produces candidates. This one produces the string the model actually reads, and it is the only plane whose output is measured directly by the objective function the whole arc is optimising: answer accuracy per token of assembled context. `get_context_card()` already assembles recent working memory for a thread with an optional pluggable `Summarizer`, per-type minimums via `min_results_by_type`, and backfill via `_relevant_with_backfill()` — the skeleton is right. What it lacks is any notion of cost.

**A. There is no token budget, so there is no packing problem being solved.** Selection today is by count and type, not by value against a budget. The correct framing is 0/1 knapsack over (value, token cost) pairs — solvable exactly in O(n x B), which is affordable at our scale but unnecessary: greedy by score-density (`score_i / tokens_i`) is (1 - 1/e)-optimal for the monotone submodular objective that MMR-style value functions induce (Nemhauser, Wolsey & Fisher, 1978), which is a strong enough guarantee that the exact solver is not worth its complexity. The existing per-type floors survive as constraints on the greedy pass.

**B. Ordering is free and we are not doing it.** Given the U-shaped position curve — accuracy highest at the beginning and end of the context, degrading >30% in the middle — the correct arrangement puts the highest-value records at the start *and* the end and buries low-value material in the middle. This costs one sort and zero tokens. It is the single cheapest item in the entire seven-epic arc.

**C. Prefix stability is a hard requirement, not a nicety, and it constrains B.** Latent/KV-cache reuse only pays off if the stable portion of the card is byte-identical across turns. If the assembled card reshuffles every turn — which naive re-ranking by fresh scores would guarantee — the cache never hits and the cost saving evaporates. The rule is: stable long-term block first and byte-identical while its contents are unchanged, volatile working-memory block last. This is in tension with pure U-curve optimisation and the resolution needs to be explicit rather than emergent.

**D. Provenance has to survive the last hop.** EPIC-27 gives every record an origin, a trust tier, and an edge to its sources; EPIC-32 makes promotion decisions on that basis. None of it reaches the model unless the rendered card carries it. A card that presents a tier-0 quarantined memory and a tier-3 operator assertion in identical prose has discarded the governance plane's entire output at the point of use.

**E. The metric that judges every other epic lives here.** Accuracy-per-1K-assembled-tokens is not currently computed anywhere. `benchmarks/quality/` measures IR metrics and LLM-judged quality, `benchmarks/latency_cost/` measures cost, and the composite scoring model from EPIC-20 (UNI-3) exists to combine such things — but the specific ratio that this arc claims to be optimising is not among them. Until ASMB-6 lands, no story in EPIC-27..33 can honestly claim to have improved the thing the research doc says we are improving.

**Scope boundary:** assembly and rendering only. Which candidates exist is EPIC-29; whether they are temporally valid is EPIC-30; whether they are trusted is EPIC-32. This plane decides which of the survivors fit and in what order.

**Depends on:** EPIC-29 RTRV-5 (MMR) and RTRV-6 (score components) for a value signal worth packing against; EPIC-32 GOV-1 for tiers worth rendering. ASMB-6 should land *early* despite being listed last, because it is the measuring instrument for everything else.
